en.title: Largest Server Ring With Adjacent Differences At Most 1 After Rearranging
en.description:
Delete some elements from an integer array; the remaining elements can be rearranged freely into a ring in which every pair of adjacent elements, including the first and last, has an absolute difference ≤1. Find the maximum number of elements kept. Equal values can be used as many times as they occur, and no elements can be added.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O, editorial and tests; missing original bounds and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the statement.
en.input: The first line contains n and the second line contains n integers. The original statement gives no value bounds; on this site 1≤n≤200000, −10^9≤value≤10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The three answers are 3, 4 and 1. The source's first example says 4, but its explanation conjures up an extra 2; with the given array at most 3 can be kept. In the second example, 1,2,3,2 does form a ring of length 4.
hints: Count frequencies and sort by value. A valid range of values must be consecutive, with every interior value appearing at least twice and each endpoint at least once. Scan the right end: restart at a gap between values, and when the previous value has frequency 1, make it the new left end; maintain the window's total frequency and the maximum.
